parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file passes: it implements a domain service holding a business rule, and everything it does belongs in the domain layer. The rule is all-or-nothing stock reservation, where every consolidated line is validated with product.assertCanReserve before any stock is changed. It also releases stock and raises a domain NotFoundError when a product is missing. It loads and saves products only through ProductRepository, which is an interface declared in the domain layer (src/domain/product/ProductRepository.ts), not a concrete persistence technology. It contains no SQL, ORM, HTTP, transport, framework or transaction-management code. Calling save() on a domain repository interface from a domain service is a normal domain pattern, not misplaced persistence logic. Someone could argue that coordinating saves belongs in the application layer, but going through an abstract domain port does not move infrastructure work into the domain. Application use cases (PlaceOrderUseCase, CancelOrderUseCase) inject this service, which fits its role as a domain service.
